38 DISCOVERIES · ONE LAKEFRONT

Follow your curiosity.

A hidden pocket of birdsong. A grand old beach house. A skyline you’ve never seen quite this way. There’s a place for every kind of wander.

BEACH

Sand, sky & a place to pause.

On the trail

Kathy Osterman Beach

A generous crescent of pale sand, neighborhood picnics, and a horizon that seems to go on forever.

Locals also call this Hollywood Beach, after the nearby avenue.

Check the Park District’s daily swimming status and posted lifeguard hours.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: Paul R. Burley · CC BY-SA 4.0 ↗

On the trail

Foster Beach

Lawn becomes sand, sand becomes lake. Foster is an easy place to let a short stop become an afternoon.

The beach is part of Lincoln Park’s long North Side landscape.

Use designated beach access paths and check daily swimming conditions.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Photo: Alanscottwalker · CC BY 3.0 ↗

Via a connector

Montrose Beach

An expansive beach where volleyball nets and lake breezes give way to protected dunes and bird habitat.

Montrose’s dunes and neighboring sanctuary create an unusually rich urban habitat.

Respect fenced nesting areas. Dogs are allowed only in the designated dog-friendly area.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: User:JeremyA · CC BY-SA 2.5 ↗

On the trail

North Avenue Beach

The Chicago postcard comes into focus: sand, volleyball courts, a ship-shaped beach house, and towers beyond.

The beach house’s silhouette evokes an ocean liner.

Slow down at beach crossings. Swimming and concessions have seasonal schedules.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: King of Hearts · CC BY-SA 3.0 ↗

On the trail

Oak Street Beach

The Gold Coast meets the sand. Few places put beach towels and skyscrapers quite this close together.

The shoreline bends dramatically here toward the downtown waterfront.

The exposed lake edge can be affected by wind and waves. Follow signs and official notices.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: Adam Jones, Ph.D. · CC BY-SA 3.0 ↗

On the trail

Ohio Street Beach

A small pocket of sand tucked beside Streeterville, with Navy Pier just around the corner.

Ohio Street Beach sits beside the peninsula containing Olive Park.

Check official beach conditions; watch for swimmers and pedestrians at beach approaches.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

Margaret T. Burroughs Beach

At 31st Street, turn back toward the city: the skyline stretches across the water beyond sand and sailboats.

The beach honors artist, educator, and DuSable Museum co-founder Margaret T. Burroughs.

Also called 31st Street Beach. Check official swimming conditions and signed neighborhood connections.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

Oakwood Beach

An open stretch of South Side sand, with room to pause between Burnham Park’s longer trail sections.

Oakwood Beach is reached from the 41st Street area.

Use the designated neighborhood connector and check current swimming conditions.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

57th Street Beach

Hyde Park’s sweep of sand, a short distance from the Point and the grand museum across the drive.

The beach sits near the northern edge of Jackson Park.

Use signed crossings for inland destinations and check daily swimming conditions.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

63rd Street Beach

A generous beach and a Classical Revival pavilion bring a graceful sense of arrival to the southern shore.

Completed in 1919, the beach house has open-air galleries designed to catch lake breezes.

Check beach conditions and seasonal facility access before visiting.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: User:TonyTheTiger · CC BY-SA 3.0 ↗

NATURE

A quieter kind of Chicago.

Nearby detour

Cricket Hill

A rare little rise in a famously flat city, with grass underfoot and wide sky overhead.

The grassy hill sits inland of Montrose Beach in Lincoln Park.

Reach it on local park paths; expect people enjoying the slopes.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Nearby detour

Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary

Step into the Magic Hedge. The skyline recedes, and the smallest movement in the leaves becomes the main event.

More than 300 bird species have been recorded in the sanctuary and adjacent dunes.

Explore on foot, stay on marked paths, and observe birds at a distance.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: peterwchen · CC BY 4.0 ↗

Nearby detour

North Pond

A quiet loop of water and reeds with neighborhood towers reflected among the trees.

The pond is inland in Lincoln Park, west of the lakefront route.

Use designated park paths and roadway crossings for this inland detour.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Nearby detour

Alfred Caldwell Lily Pool

Layered limestone, native planting, and a still pool make a small world within the city.

Alfred Caldwell’s Prairie-style landscape is a National Historic Landmark.

Check the Lincoln Park Conservancy’s current access information before your detour.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Via a connector

Maggie Daley Park

A playful downtown landscape of climbing, skating, and paths that rise and turn among the lawns.

The curving BP Pedestrian Bridge connects this park to Millennium Park.

Activities have their own hours, reservations, and age requirements.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Nearby detour

Northerly Island

Prairie planting, water on both sides, and a skyline that grows quieter as you head south.

This peninsula formerly held Meigs Field airport.

This is an out-and-back detour, not the through trail. Follow current park and event access signs.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

Burnham Park

Long lawns, lake breezes, and an uninterrupted sense of the city stretching south.

Much of this lakefront park was created through landfill and successive public works projects.

Bring water and plan your access point before choosing a longer section.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Via a connector

Promontory Point

A peninsula of mature trees and limestone steps, with the city a distant silhouette across the lake.

Alfred Caldwell designed the Point’s Prairie-style landscape in 1937.

The outer stone edge is uneven and exposed to waves. Stay on open paths and follow signs.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: Danielbv~enwiki · CC BY-SA 4.0 ↗

Nearby detour

Jackson Park & Wooded Island

Lagoons, birdsong, and the Garden of the Phoenix reveal a quieter, inland chapter of the lakefront.

Jackson Park was a principal site of the 1893 World’s Columbian Exposition.

Osaka Garden is an inland detour. Follow designated crossings and posted garden access rules.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: JulDer Wiki · CC BY 4.0 ↗

HARBOR

Follow the masts.

Nearby detour

Montrose Harbor

A sheltered curl of water, a forest of masts, and an ever-changing view of boats slipping out to the lake.

The harbor sits on the sheltered side of the Montrose peninsula.

Use the public paths; marina docks have separate access rules.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

Belmont Harbor

Follow the long curve of the harbor past sailboats, lawns, and the towers of Lakeview.

Belmont is one of the harbors in Chicago’s public lakefront harbor system.

Keep trail crossings and dock entrances clear when stopping for the view.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: TheWxResearcher · CC BY-SA 4.0 ↗

On the trail

Diversey Harbor

An inland basin threaded with boats and framed by Lincoln Park’s green canopy.

A narrow channel connects the harbor to Lake Michigan.

Follow signed paths around the channel and bridges. Dock access is restricted.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Photo: edward stojakovic from Portland, OR, United States · CC BY 2.0 ↗

On the trail

DuSable Harbor

Just south of the river mouth, sailboat masts make a delicate foreground for the downtown towers.

The harbor is named for Jean Baptiste Point DuSable.

Follow the signed downtown trail connections; docks are separate from public paths.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

Monroe Harbor

A broad mooring field turns the lake into a scattering of white sails beside Grant Park.

Monroe’s boats use a mooring-field layout rather than rows of continuous docks.

Enjoy the view from the public shoreline and leave harbor service access clear.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

Burnham Harbor

A long sheltered basin between the museums, Northerly Island, and the South Side lakefront.

Burnham Harbor forms part of Chicago’s public harbor system.

Use public shoreline routes and follow event-day directions around Museum Campus.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

On the trail

31st Street Harbor

A modern marina brings boats, promenades, and a fresh perspective on the southern skyline.

The harbor opened in 2012 as an addition to Chicago’s lakefront harbor system.

Use public promenades and keep marina gates and access routes clear.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

LANDMARK

Stories written in the skyline.

On the trail

Ardmore Avenue

Your north-to-south journey begins where Edgewater meets Lake Michigan. The whole shoreline lies ahead.

The official northern end of the Lakefront Trail is Ardmore Avenue.

Find the signed walking and cycling paths at the beach approach.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Nearby detour

Lincoln Park Zoo

Trade the long horizon for an afternoon among the zoo’s historic grounds and animal habitats.

General admission to Lincoln Park Zoo is free.

Check official hours and visitor policies. Reach the zoo using designated inland connections.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Nearby detour

Navy Pier

Follow the pier east and watch the city become a skyline. A Ferris wheel, gardens, and cultural spaces line the way.

Opened in 1916 as Municipal Pier, this 3,300-foot structure was renamed Navy Pier in 1927.

The through trail passes the landward side. Check venue hours, tickets, and bicycle rules separately.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA · CC BY-SA 2.0 ↗

Via a connector

Millennium Park

Cloud Gate, the Pritzker Pavilion, and Lurie Garden bring art and landscape into the heart of downtown.

Millennium Park is an inland destination, connected to Maggie Daley Park by the BP Bridge.

Allow time for the detour and designated crossings; park entrances can be busy.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Via a connector

Buckingham Fountain

Rose-colored stone and sculpted water give Grant Park its grand, lake-facing centerpiece.

The Clarence F. Buckingham Memorial Fountain was dedicated in 1927.

Fountain displays are seasonal. Check the official schedule and use designated crossings.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: Diego Delso · CC BY-SA 3.0 ↗

Nearby detour

Field Museum

A monumental limestone museum guards stories of the natural world, just inland from the water.

The museum grew out of collections assembled around the 1893 World’s Columbian Exposition.

Plan tickets and hours separately; allow several hours for an indoor visit.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: SarahLucciaLynch · CC BY 4.0 ↗

Nearby detour

Shedd Aquarium

The lake wraps around this grand aquarium, where campus paths open onto wide-water views.

Shedd Aquarium opened in 1930.

Check tickets and hours for entry. Outdoor campus paths can be explored separately.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Photo: Djngsf · CC BY-SA 4.0 ↗

Nearby detour

Adler Planetarium

At the end of the peninsula, a copper dome meets the sky and the whole city gathers across the water.

Opened in 1930, Adler was the first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere.

The skyline view is outdoors. Museum entry requires separate tickets and planning.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: David Ohmer from Cincinnati, USA · CC BY 2.0 ↗

Nearby detour

Soldier Field

Stone colonnades and a modern stadium bowl mark the southern edge of Museum Campus.

The stadium’s historic colonnades remain a prominent lakefront landmark.

Check event schedules and pedestrian directions; access differs on event days.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Via a connector

Griffin Museum of Science and Industry

The surviving Palace of Fine Arts from the 1893 fair is now a monumental home for science and discovery.

The building began as the Palace of Fine Arts at the World’s Columbian Exposition.

Check admission and hours; use designated park and lakefront connections.

On the map ↗Visitor information ↗

Nearby detour

South Shore Cultural Center

A former country club, now a cultural landmark, set among lawns and a long view of the lake.

The cultural center occupies the former South Shore Country Club.

Building hours and event access differ from park access. Follow public paths.

On the map ↗The story ↗

Photo: Daniel X. O'Neil from USA · CC BY 2.0 ↗

On the trail

71st Street · The southern end

Eighteen miles of lakefront behind you. A whole city of discoveries to come back for.

71st Street is the official southern endpoint of the Lakefront Trail.

Plan onward travel separately from the trail, using current transit or street navigation.
